mutant.description: The claim this face stands on is that a token signed by the PREVIOUS key is accepted while a token signed by NEITHER slot is refused. The reading that would make that TRUE ON THE TEST AND FALSE ON THE SYSTEM is a fallback branch that swallows the second verification failure and returns a decoded payload regardless -- a two-slot read that has become an accept-anything read, which every positive assertion in the suite would still pass.
mutant.expected: With the fallback branch mutated to swallow the previous-key failure and return a decoded payload regardless, S10B-AC1's negative control -- 'a token signed by a key in NEITHER slot is REFUSED' -- must FAIL, and every positive assertion must still pass. If the suite stayed green the control would be certifying nothing.
mutant.observed: 16 passed, 1 FAILED, rc=1, and the failing assertion was exactly S10B-AC1's negative control. Restored: 17 of 17, rc=0. OTHER CONTROLS RUN ON THIS FACE, recorded here because the schema allows no separate field for them: (1) S10B-AC2's NAIVE INSTRUMENT WAS FALSIFIED BY ITS OWN CONTROL -- REPORT Duration showed textbook TTL-periodic spikes on the new code, but the same measurement on the PRE-DEPLOY code (6687s of environment life, 96 invocations) returned 21 spikes, and under that code the JWT cache had no TTL and could re-read at most once per environment; cause is a SECOND 300s cache at originVerify.mjs:39, so the criterion was re-graded on CloudTrail, which carries the secretId and discriminates (row Z-S155). (2) DEPLOYED-ARTIFACT negatives: 'publicKey) return publicKey' reads 0 in the authorizer zip; 'cachedPublicKey' and 'cacheExpiry' both read 0 in the edge zip. (3) LIVE-PATH discriminators: OPTIONS /v1/market/rsi 200 against the nine 403s; the same route with no Authorization header 401 because API Gateway never invokes the Lambda. (4) EDGE health: a working edge generates its own 401 while a broken one yields 502/503, and the BOGUS-bearer arm ('error=invalid signature' on Version 19) is the load-bearing one. (5) PLAN-ZERO control: the post-apply 0-diff claim for portal_authorizer was probed against the PRE-APPLY plan, which returns 1. (6) PUSH-STATE control: the origin tip tested against origin/SITEZ reads ON ORIGIN. (7) WAF: this seat's first read of three '- rule -> null' blocks as a rule STRIPPING was WRONG; counting both halves gives 3 removals and 3 additions of the same names (a SET replacement), and the live ACL carries the same 6 rules at the same priorities after the apply. (8) THE PIN TRAP was EXHIBITED, not merely avoided: after the function apply published version 19 Active, the LIVE distribution still read auth-validator-edge:18 on 24 behaviors; the distribution apply moved it to :19 on 24 with :18 on ZERO. comp-routes cannot catch this -- it reads the qualified_arn REFERENCE in the locals block and cannot see the ignore_changes that defeats it.

(a) The nine-route probe was run THREE times -- pre-deploy baseline, post-authorizer, post-edge -- with identical results and identical controls. (c) S10B-AC2's re-read was measured on TWO different planes: the function's own REPORT Duration and the Secrets Manager control plane via CloudTrail.
